title: I've been building a 3D drone racing game with ChatGPT. Would love feedback on the gameplay and where to take it next.
author: Swimming_Ask3859
selftext:
I've been working on a browser-based 3D drone racing game called REDLINE, using ChatGPT throughout the development process.

It started as a pretty basic flying prototype, but I've gradually turned it into a racing game with a canyon environment, AI opponents, multiple camera modes, weapons, checkpoints, and a full racing HUD. I've also started integrating room-code multiplayer using Supabase.

One of the biggest things I've learned is that generating the initial code is much easier than making everything actually feel good. Getting the drone handling right, improving the environment, fixing collision problems, and making the interface readable while flying have taken a lot of iteration. I've had to keep reviewing what the AI produced, identifying specific problems, and working through fixes.

The game is still an early build, and multiplayer needs more real-world testing.

You can try it here: [https://redlin3.vercel.app](https://redlin3.vercel.app/)

I'd really appreciate feedback on a few things:

* Does the flying actually feel fun, or is the movement too awkward?
* How do the environment, drone, and racing HUD look?
* What feels unfinished or immediately needs improvement?
* Would you want to race other people in this, or does it need something fundamentally different?
* Where would you take the project next?

I'm especially interested in feedback from people who've built games using AI coding tools. What problems did you run into once your prototype started becoming a larger project?

Criticism is welcome. I'd much rather know what needs fixing than keep polishing the wrong things.
